newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official silent on possible Iraq strike.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official silent on possible Iraq strike.

text.p: A U.S. defence official on Tuesday refused to confirm or deny a German newspaper report that the United States was considering a possible cruise missile strike against Iraq over Baghdad's alleged refusal to comply with United Nations sanctions.
"As a matter of standing policy, we don't discuss future operations," said the official in response to questions.

But the official, who asked not to be identified, said the United States agreed with an analysis by chief U.N. inspector Rolf Ekeus that Iraq still possessed an operational Scud missile force of between 18 and 25 missiles.
"Iraq is not allowed to build missiles under U.N. sanctions" voted after the 1991 Gulf War, the official said.

"We agree with his (Ekeus') assessment and continue to support U.N. Special Commission efforts to insure that Iraq is in compliance with applicable U.N. Security Council resolutions," the official said.

The German newspaper Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ) reported that U.N. inspectors had discovered Iraq has continued to develop missiles in contravention of U.N. resolutions, and said the United States was contemplating a possible missile strike against Iraq.

In an advance release from Wednesday's edition, the newspaper said the United States could make a decision this week on whether to launch a Tomahawk missile strike at Iraq. It sourced its report to "American security sources."
The United States has launched three such Tomahawk strikes against Iraq since the war ended.

The FAZ said U.N. inspectors who were in Iraq between Jan. 5 and 23 found evidence, according to American sources, that Iraq was continuing to develop missiles with a range of around 1,000 miles (1,600 kms).

The FAZ also said U.N. inspectors had been "massively obstructed" during their recent visit. It said Ekeus had written to Iraqi Prime Minister Tariq Aziz on Jan. 13 telling him that Iraq was contravening U.N. resolutions and this would have consequences.
